newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says vets P&O /Nedlloyd merger.
newsitem.headline: EU says vets P&O /Nedlloyd merger.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it was probing the proposed merger of the container shipping businesses of Britain's Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co and Royal Nedlloyd NV of the Netherlands.

It said the deal was submitted for clearance on November 19 under European Union merger rules which ban creation or strengthening of dominant positions. The Commission has a month from that date to decide whether to clear the operation or start an in-depth four-month investigation.
Under the terms of the deal, P&O and Nedlloyd would create a joint venture called P&O Nedlloyd Container Line Ltd. This is the first merger in the container shipping business.

The two companies are members of the Trans-Atlantic Conference Agreement (TACA), a liner conference for the regular sea transport of containers which the Commission has qualified as "unlawful" and threatened to fine if it is not changed. This is because of TACA provisions relating to inland transport rate fixing.
European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has declined to comment on whether he would be using the merger as leverage to obtain the long-sought changes to TACA.
